newsitem.title: USA: Donna Karan sees loss for 1997, president resigns.
newsitem.headline: Donna Karan sees loss for 1997, president resigns.

text.p: Struggling fashion design company Donna Karan International Inc. on Thursday said losses widened to $14.7 million in the second quarter, predicted further losses and announced the resignation of its president and chief operating officer.
The resignation of Stephen Ruzow, effective immediately, marked the second major management change at Donna Karan in less than a week.

On Monday, Donna Karan named John Idol, an executive from Polo Ralph Lauren Corp., to take over as the company's chief executive officer. Idol will replace company founder Donna Karan, who will give up the CEO's post but remain chairman and chief designer.
The company said Ruzow also would resign as a company director but would stay on as a consultant for the next six months.

Donna Karan International reported a net loss of $14.7 million, or 68 cents a share, compared with a loss of $4.15 million, or 19 cents a share in the year-ago quarter. Sales totalled $111 million for the quarter, down from $117.6 million last year.
The company said it expects to report a loss of 55 cents a share or greater for the year, excluding potential additional charges.

For the first six months of the year, Donna Karan posted a loss of $13.9 million, or 64 cents a share, on sales of $269.8 million, vs. a profit of $7.6 million, or 35 cents a share, on sales of $277 million in 1996.

The company said the results reflected a difficult retail environment, disappointing sales for its DKNY Women's and Donna Karan New York Men's spring collections and previously announced charges associated with restructuring and cost containment programmes.

"Clearly, we are extremely disappointed with our second quarter results, said Chairman Donna Karan. "Our board of directors took decisive action earlier this week in the appointment of John Idol ... to begin to address the company's performance issues."
The announcements came after the close of trading Thursday. Donna Karan stock fell 44 cents to $14 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
